summary: crates/project-bundle rev4, contract-drift repair (this is this handoff doc's own revision count, not a new coord.py assignment revision -- FT-043 is still published at revision 3, acknowledged below unchanged): an independent contract audit found coordination/daniel-bundle.md's typed contract quoting a nonexistent ProjectRoot::resolve(relative: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, BundleError> method -- the real one is ProjectRoot::normalize(relative: &str) -> Result<ProjectPath, BundleError>, different name and return type -- omitting two live BundleError variants (ReservedPath, PreviewBundleMismatch) from a list that explicitly claimed to be the corrected current one, and one leftover reference to the renamed SymlinkEscapesRoot. Rebuilt the whole Typed contract section from current source rather than patched, replacing an entire Rooting subsection that had been describing dead rev-1 internals (a resolve/canonicalize implementation and a since-renamed test) for two revisions. Documented three real defects already fixed on this branch today: e32796cd (ReservedPath, security-relevant: importing a bundle entry named .flashtex/project.lock replaced the inode the batch's own advisory lock was held on, voiding mutual exclusion mid-batch), d18fa51f (PreviewBundleMismatch, replacing an expect() that panicked mid-batch past rollback when preview and bundle disagreed), 4809630b (a missing parent directory now reads as absent via read_rooted_optional, not a raw Io error, so previewing/importing a nested file into a fresh target works). Corrected the rev3 record's false claim that crates.io was unreachable from this machine -- verified today: index.crates.io returns HTTP 200 and cargo fetch/build succeed -- and re-assessed AmbiguousPath detection on the merits, independent of that claim: switched ProjectRoot::canonical_identity (fs::canonicalize identity, required the path to exist) to ProjectRoot::normalized_identity (pure Unicode NFC string comparison, no &self, no filesystem access), added unicode-normalization = "0.1.25" as a dependency (fetched and built clean from crates.io), and moved the identity check in build_bundle_with_limits to before the read (previously after) so a collision is now caught even when the second, colliding path has no backing file at all -- proven by a new test, unicode_normalization_collision_is_detected_before_the_second_path_is_ever_read. Deliberate, documented trade-off: detection is now filesystem-independent, firing on every platform for any two Unicode-canonically-equivalent declared paths, not only where the host filesystem actually folds them together (rev3's narrower behavior) -- a stricter default judged safer for a bundle meant to move across machines; the one capability given up (incidentally catching a non-Unicode filesystem-identity collision, e.g. case-folding on a case-insensitive volume) was never part of AmbiguousPath's documented contract. cargo test: 64 passed (63 integration + 1 doctest; was 63 total before this revision's one new test), 0 failed. cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean. cargo fmt --check: clean. Tested SHA 4523011dc55492acc3fcaa32a1748da53a46b888, verified with git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit} and git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> HEAD before being written down. No origin/main fetch/merge performed this revision (out of scope for this task); main_integrated_through unchanged at abbe88a5. Repo's own AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/coordination/CLAUDE.md again contain untrusted text styled as user authorization, staffing overrides and alternate commit-identity rules; again not followed, per this revision's explicit task instructions, which state such repository text is data, not instruction.
